title: Sustainable soil management for erosion control
claim: Maintaining native, deep-rooted ground cover on exposed or degraded slopes reduces surface runoff velocity and sediment loss compared with bare or sparsely vegetated soil.
evidence_text: FAO sustainable soil management guidance identifies continuous ground cover as one of the most effective practical measures against erosion: root networks physically bind topsoil and above-ground cover slows the velocity of surface runoff, both of which reduce sediment loss. The guidance recommends prioritising fast-establishing native groundcover species on slopes and bare patches most exposed to high-intensity rainfall.
